after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨{e}^{2-t},\,3+{t}^{4}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=2.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2-t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3+{t}^{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨-{e}^{2-t},\,4{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{2-t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{2-t},\,12{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=2,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(2) & =⟨{e}^{2-2},12(2)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,48⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2

The velocity vector v=⟨u,v⟩ of a particle P at time t is given by v=⟨3t−1,2t+1⟩,t>0. Calculate the acceleration vector a at time t=4.

a
a(4)=⟨3,13⟩
b
a(4)=⟨4,13⟩
c
a(4)=⟨4,13⟩
d
a(4)=⟨11,3⟩
e
a(4)=⟨3,3⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector: a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(3t−1),ddt(2t+1)⟩=⟨3,12t+1⟩

Finally, to find the acceleration at time t=4, we substitute t=4 into the above: a(4)=⟨3,12(4)+1⟩=⟨3,19⟩=⟨3,13⟩

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Acceleration of a Particle at a Given Moment Given Its Velocity Vector
content.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨3t-1,\sqrt{2t+1}⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=4.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t-1),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2t+1})⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\frac{1}{\sqrt{2t+1}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=4,$ we substitute $t=4$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(4) & =⟨3,\frac{1}{\sqrt{2(4)+1}}⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\frac{1}{\sqrt{9}}⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\frac{1}{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
The position vector $r(t)$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r(t)=⟨4t-{t}^{3},2{t}^{2}+t⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t-{t}^{3}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}+t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4-3{t}^{2},4t+1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4-3{t}^{2}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-6t,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$
